artworks.title: Saturn and Philyra
artworks.description: Cronus (Saturn), transformed into a stallion to hide from Rhea, couples with the Oceanid Philyra — the union that will bear the centaur Chiron. Renaissance mythography loved this equine disguise; the print keeps Philyra as mother of the wisest of the Centaurs.

artworks.title: Saturn in the guise of a horse being suckled by the nymph Philyra
artworks.description: A Metropolitan Museum engraving titles the scene outright: Saturn as a horse nursed or attended by Philyra. The Oceanid of Pelion is fixed as the nymph of Cronus' equine metamorphosis and Chiron's conception.

artworks.title: Saturn and the Nymph Philyra
artworks.description: Dutch print culture restages Saturnus with Philyra — the Oceanid whose shame at bearing a half-horse child (in some tellings) drives her to become a linden tree, while Chiron remains the immortal tutor of heroes.

artworks.title: Saturn and Philyra
artworks.description: Parmigianino's drawing (Royal Collection) isolates the nymph with the horse-formed Titan — Mannerist line for the myth that makes Philyra mother of Chiron on Mount Pelion.

popCulture.title: Chiron
popCulture.description: Philyra's son by Cronus is the wise Centaur — the Oceanid remembered whenever the tutor of Achilles and Asclepius is named.

popCulture.title: Philyra (mythology)
popCulture.description: Oceanid daughter of Oceanus; by Cronus in horse-form she bore Chiron — and in some accounts became the linden (philyra) that still bears her name.
